TWO urls as of P6.5 (#1814), with SEPARATE budgets — a single `assertions` block would have applied /login's 7000ms LCP to the public page, which is the number this phase exists to beat rather than to inherit. Measured 2026-10-15: this gate covered ONE of 395 live routes, and the one route P6.5 promises an LCP target for was not it.

/f/{handle} starts on `warn` DELIBERATELY. Its real LCP has never been measured, and the repo's rule for this file is that a budget is a REGRESSION GATE set just above a known-stable number, not an aspirational target asserted before anybody looked. The 2500ms in #1814's title is a goal; the `error` gate goes in once the three-run median is in a report. Asserting 2500 now would either pass by luck or fail a PR for a number nobody had measured.

assertMatrix.//: Re-baselined 2026-10-16 for #2002, replacing the 2026-07-13 note that described the `simulate` regime. #1980 switched to `throttlingMethod: devtools`, so these numbers are MEASURED, not modelled, and the old note's claim that 'simulate throttling is host-independent so CI matches local' no longer applies. LCP IS DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED HERE. Its element is the PWA install banner (InstallPrompt.tsx, a mobile-only fixed overlay rendered after hydration): Render Delay was 6225ms of a 6266ms LCP while the sign-in FORM painted at FCP 2080ms. A budget on it gated when a promotional bar appears, not when the page becomes usable, and it would move whenever the install-prompt logic changed. Owner ruling 2026-10-16: gate what a person waits for. FCP 2600 and TBT 1000 are derived from two jobs, 6 runs: FCP medians 2080 and 2041 (7ms... 39ms apart), worst single sample 2266; TBT medians 461 and 454 (7ms apart), worst single sample 853. Each budget sits ABOVE the worst single sample, because the assertion is on a median of three and two bad samples can move it. TBT is 1000 and not 900 on purpose: the previous note records a flake at exactly 900 ('a median of 900.2 against a 900 budget'). That was the simulate regime where TBT ran 900-2630ms, so 900 is numerically safe now at a 457ms median — but reusing the one number with a documented flake history invites the next reader to assume nothing changed. The old note's named lever is STILL UNPULLED: /login ships the full operator catalogue, because PUBLIC_SURFACE_PREFIXES is ['/f'] only, so an unauthenticated sign-in page serialises all 5787 keys. #1960 split the catalogue but /login is not on the public surface. Filed separately.

The public farm page. MEASURED 2026-10-15, FIVE runs with median aggregation — the first trustworthy figure for this page: LCP 3191 ms, FCP 1679 ms, Speed Index 1679 ms, TBT 286 ms, CLS 0.000, performance 87. This tree has the client chrome removed (#1874) and NOT the heading-font preload (#1877). `aggregationMethod` is set PER ENTRY and that is not a style choice: at the top level lhci refuses with 'Cannot use assertMatrix with other options', which is how the first attempt at this fix failed. Without it the gate passed an LCP of 3672 ms against a 3200 ms error budget (#1878) — the default is not the per-metric median this file's reporter prints. Five runs, not three. Two 3-run medians of the SAME commit came back 296 ms apart (3672 and 3376), so three samples cannot separate a change from the runner here. /login is documented below as stable to +/-25 ms over three; this page is not, and reading it as though it were produced two claims that had to be retracted — a 905 ms gain for #1874 and a 942 ms loss for #1877, neither supported. 3600 is the 5-run median plus ~13%, matching the headroom /login's gate uses over its own measurement. P6.5 wants 2500 ms and this is 691 ms short; the gate is a regression bound, not the target. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-16, five runs: LCP median 3046 ms (min 2732, max 3188, spread 456), FCP 1070 ms, TBT 239 ms, performance 90-92. That is 145 ms better than the 2026-10-15 figure with nothing aimed at this page in between, which is the spread talking, not a gain. The gate is deliberately NOT tightened to the new median. 3600 sits 412 ms above the observed max, roughly one spread; median+13% would be 3442, only 254 ms above that max and so BELOW the noise. A regression gate has to clear the instrument's own spread or it fails on a quiet commit, and this page's spread is the one documented reason this file uses five runs instead of three. WHY 2500 ms IS NOT PURSUED THROUGH THIS GATE (#1814) Measured 2026-10-16 on a local build whose chunk hashes reproduce CI's exactly (41151-b546513852e0f60e.js is the same file in both). /f/{handle} loads 1,023,621 raw bytes of JavaScript, and 862,065 of them (84%) are `rootMainFiles` from .next/build-manifest.json -- webpack, React DOM and main-app, loaded by every route in the app. No layout change, provider move or route-group split can reach that 84%: the page is hydrated, so the framework ships. The theoretical ceiling of such a refactor is the other 16%, most of which is Next's route runtime and this page's own code; the only provider code proven to leak in is sonner's 8,895 bytes, 0.9% (#1971). The LCP element is `

` -- the about text -- with phases TTFB 458 ms, Load Delay 0, Load Time 0, Render Delay 2274 ms. The delay is modelled main-thread work, not bytes for that element. Unthrottled, the same traces report observedFirstVisualChange 145 ms and observedLastVisualChange 191 ms with every request complete by 302 ms: the page is visually finished in under a fifth of a second, and 3046 ms is what Lighthouse's simulated slow-4G plus 4x CPU model makes of it. So P6.5's LCP target is settled on FIELD data rather than here. `/api/metrics` carries `surface` since #1962, so a per-surface p75 becomes readable once agrent ships its container logs (#1940). This entry stays what it says it is: a regression bound.
